# Camera moves: Arcs and time

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_references.py from scripts/catalog.py. Edit the catalogue, then rebuild. -->

Read this file when the user wants time to freeze or stretch, a swing around the subject, or a hit shown in 2 sizes.
Each entry is 1 complete recipe. The `id` is the value for `--techniques`.

## Frozen-moment arc (bullet time)

`id: frozen_arc`

- **Plain words:** Time almost stops and the camera sweeps part of the way around the subject.
- **Camera movement:** a fast, smooth arc of about 130 degrees around the subject: it starts behind the shoulder, passes the profile and stops at a front three-quarter view; it never reaches a view straight in front.
- **Camera placement:** at the subject's own height, the lens level, 2 to 3 m away, on one side of the action for the whole move.
- **Lens:** 35 mm. Wide enough to feel the camera travel past the background, not so wide that bodies bend at the frame edge.
- **Default light:** One hard low sun, camera facing into the light. Second choice: Low hard side sun.
- **Default grade:** Film print, deep blacks. Second choice: Bleach bypass.
- **Speed:** Frozen moment. **Length:** 2 to 3 s.
- **The viewer feels:** The viewer gets a held breath: one instant, seen from more than one side.
- **Choose it when:** One peak moment in the whole piece: the top of a jump, the instant before a landing or a hit.
- **Risks with AI video generators:**
  - A full 180 or 360 degree orbit turns faces into the lens and flips left and right on screen. Ask for about 130 degrees.
  - Generators let frozen bodies float upward. Write 'real gravity, drifting only a hand's width'.
  - The background behind the subject is invented during the move. Keep the place simple.
- **AI look it avoids:** 180 or 360 degree orbit; Floating, weightless bodies.

## Arc shot (partial orbit, real time)

`id: fast_arc`

- **Plain words:** The camera swings around the subject at normal speed, fast, and stops.
- **Camera movement:** one fast arc of about 90 degrees around the subject in real time, starting on a whip of motion blur and stopping dead on a side-on frame.
- **Camera placement:** at waist height, 2 m away, the lens level, on one side of the action.
- **Lens:** 24 mm. A wide lens close to the subject makes the swing feel fast and keeps the place in the frame.
- **Default light:** Low hard side sun. Second choice: Night, practical lights only.
- **Default grade:** Warm natural. Second choice: Muted earth tones.
- **Speed:** Real time. **Length:** 1.5 to 3 s.
- **The viewer feels:** Energy and swagger. The camera has an attitude of its own.
- **Choose it when:** An entrance, a trick, a turn: any moment that needs speed more than awe.
- **Risks with AI video generators:**
  - Generators slow an arc to a gentle drift. Write 'fast', 'real time' and where it stops.
  - A wide lens stretches faces near the frame edge. Keep faces near the middle third.
- **AI look it avoids:** Aquarium speed: slow floating camera and slow bodies; 180 or 360 degree orbit.

## Speed ramp

`id: speed_ramp`

- **Plain words:** Normal speed, a short slow-down at the best instant, then normal speed again.
- **Camera movement:** a side-on tracking move that travels with the subject at their speed.
- **Camera placement:** side-on at hip height, 4 m away, travelling parallel to the action.
- **Lens:** 50 mm. A normal lens side-on keeps body shapes true while the speed change does the work.
- **Default light:** Flat overcast daylight. Second choice: Low hard side sun.
- **Default grade:** Cool and desaturated. Second choice: Warm natural.
- **Speed:** Speed ramp. **Length:** 3 to 5 s.
- **The viewer feels:** The viewer feels the speed and then gets a clear look at the best instant.
- **Choose it when:** Sport, tricks, a jump, a throw: fast action with one peak.
- **Risks with AI video generators:**
  - Generators stay slow after the ramp. Write 'back to real time before the landing'.
  - Say exactly which instant is slow.
- **AI look it avoids:** Slow motion everywhere; Centred, front-facing subject.

## Contact insert with a ramp on contact

`id: impact_insert`

- **Plain words:** A tight shot of the instant of contact. Slow on the way in, full speed from the contact.
- **Camera movement:** locked and tight on the point of contact; at the frame of contact the frame kicks a hand's width in the direction of the force, then settles.
- **Camera placement:** exactly side-on to the line of the force, at chest height, 2 m away, never in front of a face.
- **Lens:** 85 mm. A long lens from the side isolates the contact and keeps the camera out of the action.
- **Default light:** Low hard side sun. Second choice: Night, practical lights only.
- **Default grade:** Bleach bypass. Second choice: Film print, deep blacks.
- **Speed:** Ramp on contact. **Length:** 1.5 to 2.5 s.
- **The viewer feels:** The viewer feels the contact, not only sees it.
- **Choose it when:** One decisive contact: a hit, a catch, a landing, a ball on a bat. Show the whole move in a wider shot first.
- **Risks with AI video generators:**
  - Generators add a slow wind-up. Write 'the first visible motion is the action itself'.
  - The contact goes soft or misses. Name the part that strikes, the exact target and the reaction along the line of the force.
  - Generators stretch the whole shot into slow motion. State the frame where real speed returns.
- **AI look it avoids:** Slow motion everywhere; Aquarium speed: slow floating camera and slow bodies.
